newsitem.title: UK: LME copper holds above $2,150, market seen tight.
newsitem.headline: LME copper holds above $2,150, market seen tight.

text.p: LME copper surmounted $2,150 resistance on Thursday afternoon as tightness re-emerged in the market, widening spreads again.
"All in all it looks like the market is tight again," said analyst William Adams of broker Rudolf Wolff.

The market has been worried that firm backwardations may not be backed up by fundamentals, but if there was actually a surplus of metal firm prices should have attracted it onto the market by now, he added.
Copper ended the afternoon kerb at $2,155 per tonne, up from $2,114 on Wednesday.
The premium of cash over three months rose to $103/$104 from $90 on Wednesday, reflecting borrowing, dealers said.
The next resistance area was $2,175, followed by $2,215 and $2,300, chartists said.
Technicals were looking good, but the market may lack volume as it moves into the West's slow Christmas holiday season, Adams said.
Aluminium was also looking robust, having broken through $1,546 resistance, the high of December 13.
Trade interest is good and prices are now well above the uptrend line, Adams said.
Zinc added $9 to $1,062 and tin rose $30 to $5,850.
Alloy was indicated at $1,385/90, up about $15 from Wednesday.
The next ceiling to break through was $1,570, the high of November 28. There was a band of trading between $1,600 and $1,680, the next significant peak, Adams said.
Other metals firmed with copper and aluminium.
Nickel made a good move to finish at $6,775, up $135, recovering well from 26-month lows hit on Monday.
The market would need to clear $6,950 to confirm that the rise was not merely a correction higher within a downtrend, Adams said.
Lead gained $16 to $714, convincingly breaking above a downtrend line at $699.
